summary: Sporadic evening 5xx elevation after ingress keepalive rotation causing runtime scheduling pressure
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-01 19:20 UTC LexiAI reported a persistent elevated 5xx error rate (~3-6% vs normal <0.3%) for short-text generation endpoints. Errors appeared as 502/503 from the API gateway and downstream runtime grpc failures. Impact: Customer production traffic experienced degraded success rate and increased tail latency; user retries amplified load. Environment: prod | us-east; Dedicated tenant on shared runtime pool; models: redwood-3b-v1 (primary), open-llama-13b (fallback). Steps to reproduce: 1) Send sustained concurrent short-gen requests (50-80 RPS) to /v1/generate with keepalive enabled. 2) Observe gateway 5xx error rate rising in 15-30m window during high connection churn and at ~10m intervals when ingress keepalive rotation occurs. Observed metrics & logs: - API gateway 502/503 spikes align with 10m keepalive rotation TTL at the fronting proxy. - Runtime pod logs show repeated 'uvm_page_fault' and 'gpu-driver-reset' traces at the same timestamps. - Kernel dmesg on host showed GPU UVM pagefault queues bloating followed by driver recovery. - Autoscaler briefly scaled up, then some new workers failed readiness due to kvcache lock acquisition timeouts. Initial customer-facing mitigation applied: support recommended temporarily increasing ingress keepalive from 600s -> 3600s and reducing connection churn. This lowered immediate error-floor.
comments: 2026-03-01 19:40 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Investigated initial logs with customer. Noted correlation between ingress keepalive rotation and gateway 5xx timestamps. Advised increasing keepalive TTL as temporary mitigation.

2026-03-01 20:05 UTC - Arjun Patel (SRE): Observed contiguous uvm pagefault queue growth on host nodes hosting the tenant. GPU driver reports followed by recovery. Hypothesis: short-lived connection churn + new worker warmups cause repeated GPU memory map faults and UVM thrashing under the current kernel scheduling; increases host CPU/GPU scheduler contention and causes runtime grpc failures.

2026-03-02 01:12 UTC - Priya Rao (Runtime Eng): Confirmed kvcache lock contention during worker initialization when tenant load spikes. Added instrumentation to measure kvcache wait times and UVM fault rates. Opening runtime PR to add backoff and staggered warmup for GPUs.

2026-03-02 09:30 UTC - Arjun Patel (SRE): Deployed ingress-proxy change to increase keepalive to 3600s for affected frontends and adjusted a socket-reuse setting. Early telemetry shows 5xx% reduced to baseline in the affected tenant group.

2026-03-02 14:00 UTC - Maya Chen (Support): Customer confirmed throughput and error-rate stabilized after changes; accepted temporary workaround. Customer requests ETA for permanent fix and follow-up to prevent recurrence during high-fanout events.

2026-03-03 10:00 UTC - Priya Rao (Runtime Eng): Runtime patch merged and rolled to canary: introduces staggered GPU warmup, kvcache acquisition timeouts, and graceful fallback to model-variant when UVM faults exceed threshold. See PR #1224.
2026-03-03 15:40 UTC - Arjun Patel (SRE): Full rollout completed and monitoring alert thresholds tuned. Closing ticket pending post-rollout observation window (48h).
investigation_notes: Metric correlation: 502/503 spikes align to 10m fronting proxy keepalive rotation (TTL=600s) and cluster worker churn windows.
Host-level evidence: kernel dmesg shows UVM page fault queue growth and 'NVIDIA UVM: kill process' style driver recoveries in narrow windows coincident with keepalive rotation.
Runtime traces: grpc errors during kvcache lock waits (>= 250ms) and 'prefetch cancelled' messages for tenants undergoing fanout.
Autoscaler behavior: Scale-up happened but new pods failed readiness due to extended kvcache init time, amplifying connection pressure on existing pods.

Hypothesis: Combination of ingress connection churn + parallel worker warmups causes repeated UVM pagefault storms; kernel/driver then issues GPU resets, running pods lose in-flight requests producing 502/503 and runtime exits.
resolution_summary: Deployed a two-part fix: (1) immediate mitigation - increased ingress keepalive and enabled socket reuse to reduce connection churn; (2) permanent runtime fix - staggered GPU warmup + kvcache acquisition backoff and a defensive UVM-fault threshold to trigger lightweight model-variant fallback. Both changes rolled to prod 2026-03-03. Customer reports error-rate back to baseline. Follow-up: SRE to monitor UVM fault metrics for 72h, Runtime Eng to add additional low-level metrics and a long-term plan to tune kernel UVM parameters or provide tenancy isolation guidance.
follow_up_actions: SRE: Monitor uvmpagefault_rate and kvcache_wait_ms for 72 hours; escalate if 5xx > 0.5% for tenant.
Runtime Eng: Implement additional diagnostic counters for UVM mappings and publish guidance for dedicated workloads in runbook.
Product: Communicate to LexiAI summary and recommended tenant configuration (connection reuse, pinned capacity) to avoid recurrence.
Infra: Evaluate kernel parameter tuning and NVIDIA driver recommendations (defer to infra schedule).
